Subject: Evaluation plan + marketplace procurement path (AWS private offer)

Priya / Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, I've attached an evaluation plan that maps the technical milestones to procurement checkpoints so your security and procurement teams can sign off incrementally. High-level proposal:

- Week 1–2: Integration & smoke tests (Redwood hosted eval) — no commitment; goal: validate latency and API fits.
- Week 3–4: Pilot with PII-sanitized data, automated billing on a sandbox private offer (small reserved capacity). Pricing: evaluation rate (metered) + refundable staging credit.
- Week 5–8: Ramp to production pilot under a private AWS Marketplace offer with a staged commit (30/60/90). MAP milestone hits trigger stepped discounts and committed capacity.

I've included a draft private-offer term sheet (RI_Private_Offer_Draft.pdf) and a more detailed MAP spreadsheet (MAP_milestones.xlsx). Key ask for procurement: confirm acceptance of staged-commit structure and procurement timeline so we can generate the AWS private offer and a DocuSign packet.

Next step: are you available Thursday 10am PT for a short procurement + security alignment?

Thanks,

Priya —

Great questions, summarized answers below and I've attached a worked example table inside MAP_milestones.xlsx: see tab "Pricing Worked Example". Short answers:

1) Example (3-month pilot -> production ramp):
   - Month 0 (eval): metered @ $0.08 per 1k tokens (evaluation rate)
   - Milestone 1 (Pilot go/no-go): apply 10% credit on invoice for next 30 days if throughput targets met
   - Milestone 2 (Production ramp): commit to a 6-month reserved baseline; pricing steps to effective $0.06 per 1k tokens (20% off baseline) once commit hits 70% of guaranteed throughput.
   - All numbers in MAP_milestones.xlsx are illustrative; we can refine to exact $ amounts post-call.

2) AWS private-offer fees: marketplace listing & private-offer orchestration fees are typically handled by Redwood as part of the offer creation (we absorb initial listing admin). The committed-reserve billing will flow through AWS; refunds/credits tied to MAP failure are handled per the private-offer terms — we proposed a refundable staging credit in the draft. Finance sign-off required for non-standard refund terms.

3) Marissa — can you attach the compliance pack (SOC2 report, KMS/HSM integration notes) and confirm we can include the link in the DocuSign?

I'll be on the call Thu 10am PT. Karthik is looped for pricing/commit questions.

Thanks,
Jordan
